sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:

On 08-01-2023 at about 8.00 p.m., the petitioner being a pillion rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-W- 2610, was proceeding on Parashurampura-Dharmapura road,
near Parashurampura Forest, Chitradurga, the same was ridden by the rider very carefully and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations.

At that time,
all of a sudden one passenger auto bearing No.KA-16-D-4293, driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, with high speed, came from Doddachelluru road and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Parashurampura and Chitradurga Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident he was Shepherd and earning a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- per annum.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Parashurampura Police have registered the case against the driver of the said passenger auto for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of auto- rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

It has contended that, the vehicle in question i.e. auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 is not at all involved in the alleged accident, the same has been falsely implicated in order to get wrongful gain and to make wrongful loss to respondent No.1.

The entire police records are manipulated by showing the registration number of auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 and seasoned professional have joined hands with the petitioner and manipulated the charge-sheet.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner has suppressed the true facts and colluded with the respondent No.2 and the jurisdictional police and fixed false case against the driver of auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293.

2 records there is delay in lodging complaint, the jurisdictional police have filed a false charge-sheet,
by creating a false story and implicated the present vehicle and manipulated records.

Further it is contended that, on the date of accident, the driver of auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 was not holding valid and effective driving licence.

The owner of the vehicle has allowed the said driver to drive the same, knowing fully well that he has no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and the said auto-rickshaw was not having valid permit and fitness certificate to ply in the place of accident.
Hence, there is a violation of policy conditions as well as provisions of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, as on the date of accident the driver/insured (Thippeswamy S/o Mukundappa) of the auto- rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 was holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

Further it is contended that, the auto-rickshaw bearing Reg.
No.KA-16-D-4293 was havign permit to ply the said vehicle within 10 km from Parashurampura Hobli, issued by Chitradurga RTO, valid from 05-10-2019 to 04-10-2024.
The permit was valid as on the date of accident.
Further it is contended that, the fitness certificate of said auto rickshaw was valid from 29-09-2022 to 28-09-2024.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay any compensation ordered by this Court.
For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the road traffic accident alleged to have occurred on 08-01-2023 at about 8.00 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Passenger Auto bearing Reg.

No.KA- 16-D-4293 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

13. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-16- D-4293 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

The respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the insured auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 was not at all involved in the alleged accident, the same has been falsely implicated by the petitioner, in order to get wrongful gain and to make wrongful loss to the respondents.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

They have neither adduced any evidence to establish the above contentions, nor they have produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Even, the respondents No.1 and 2 have not stepped into witness box to depose the contentions taken in their written statements on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D- 4293 and dashing the same to the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-W-2610 from opposite direction, while he was proceeding on the left side of Parashurampura- Dharmapura road.

Though, the learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 have cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-W-2610 himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part, in the cause of accident.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 12 feet wide Parashurampura- Dharmapura road, near Parashurampura Forest, Challakere Taluk, in between the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-W- 2610 and offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-16- D-4293.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-W-2610, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
On the other hand, the respondents have not produced any rebuttal evidence to show that, the said documents are false and concocted documents.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-16-D-4293 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D-4293.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 discharge summary,
Ex.P.15 OPD card and Ex.P.16 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident i.e.
1) closed traumatic comminuted right mid shaft femur fracture, 2) right neck of femur fracture with contused lacerated wound over right knee and 3) right 5th metatarsal head fracture.

The P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained the above injuries in a road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondents No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length

,
nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: 17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others

, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
18.

Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 08-01-2023 at about 8.00 p.m., on Parashurampura-Dharmapura road, near Parashurampura Forest, Challakere Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Passenger Auto bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D-4293.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of passenger auto bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D-4293 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained 1)
closed traumatic comminuted right mid shaft femur fracture, 2) right neck of femur fracture with contused lacerated wound over right knee and 3) right 5th metatarsal head fracture.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment,
attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages,
such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

sentences.text: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.14.
As per Ex.P.14, the date of birth of the petitioner is 02.08.1986.
The accident has taken place on 08- 01-2023 at about 8:00 p.m.
This clearly goes show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 37 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered 1) closed traumatic comminuted right mid shaft femur fracture, 2) right neck of femur fracture with contused lacerated wound over right knee and 3) right 5th metatarsal head fracture and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered 63% disability to his right lower limb and 31% to the whole body.

Further, the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 discharge summary, Ex.P.15 OPD card and Ex.P.16 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability as stated by him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 08-01-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 07-11-2024, which is after lapse of one year and 11 months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the follow-up treatment of the petitioner is completed and the disability assessed by him will be reduced if the petitioner undergoes further surgery for union of femur shaft.
Further he has deposed that, the fracture of neck of femur is united, but there is non-union of fracture of shaft of femur and mal- union of fracture of head of 5th metatarsal.
Further he has deposed that, there is shortening of limb.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was a shepherd and earning a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- per annum.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondents have specifically denied the same.

sentences.text: But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was a shepherd and was earning Rs.5,00,000/- per annum.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2023.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 37 years is 15.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298

sentences.text:
Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 20/100 X 15 = Rs.5,58,000/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.3,50,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 53 medical bills, as per Ex.P.9.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.1,62,753/- towards his medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,62,753/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. 1)
closed traumatic comminuted right mid shaft femur fracture, 2) right neck of femur fracture with contused lacerated wound over right knee and 3) right 5th metatarsal head fracture.
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 15 days from 9.1.2023 to 23.1.2023, in Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, as per the evidence of P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 15 days, from 9.1.2023 to 23.1.2023, in Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 15 = Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 15 days in Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 15 =
Rs.12,000/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Siddeshwaranadurga, Chitradurga District, the accident has taken place on Parashurampura-Dharmapura road, near Parashurampura Forest, Challakere Taluk, Chitradurga District and the petitioner has taken treatment at Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places

,
compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.

viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 37 years and unfortunately he has suffered 1) closed traumatic comminuted right mid shaft femur fracture, 2) right neck of femur fracture with contused lacerated wound over right knee and 3) right 5th metatarsal head fracture.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 20% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs revision surgery for achieving union, the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.50,000/-.

But,
admittedly the P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 5,58,000-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,62,753-00 3.
Pain and sufferings 50,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 15,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 12,000-00
6. Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during 46,500-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 30,000-00 Total Rs. 9,24,253-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,24,253/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
21. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D- 4293.

It is not in dispute that, the policy issued by the respondent No.1 bearing No.V9969110, in respect of offending Yathiraj N vs Future India Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125572366/
9 auto-rickshaw was valid from 24-03-2022 to 23- 03-2023.

sentences.text: As such the policy issued by the respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of said policy by the insurer/respondent No.2.

The evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that,
due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D-4293 the said accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of said vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
